clue.text: Pester old lady for Spooner's ice cream

indicators.note: Spooner's tells us to swap the opening sounds of the two words the clue gives

parts.note: to pester someone is to nag them
old lady is slang for mother, mum

explanation.surface: A child pesters their mother for an ice cream in a muddled way.
explanation.walkthrough: NAG MUM with first letters swapped gives MAG NUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnum is a well-known brand of chocolate-coated ice cream on a stick.

clue.text: Horse broken by melancholy playwright

indicators.note: broken by means the horse word is split open by the next word

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
low means down or melancholy

explanation.surface: A horse is tamed by a gloomy dramatist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken by' is a container signal: the horse is broken open, not tamed, with the gloomy word set inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Marlowe was an Elizabethan dramatist, author of Doctor Faustus.

clue.text: Booty-lifting trousers quietly getting stares

indicators.note: trousers as a verb means pockets, so the reversed loot takes this letter in
lifting in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: swag is booty or loot
P is the musical abbreviation piano, quietly

explanation.surface: Trousers that lift the buttocks attract gawkers.
explanation.walkthrough: SWAG upwards is GAWS, and it pockets P: GAW-P-S. 'trousers' is a verb, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To gawp is to gape or gaze foolishly.

clue.text: Officiated mud wrestling entered by 10 soldiers

indicators.note: entered by means the jumbled letters take the next pieces inside
wrestling suggests a tussle, so the letters of mud are thrown about

parts.note: 10 points to the answer at 10 across, a private eye, a private investigator or PI
RE is the Royal Engineers, a body of soldiers

explanation.surface: A referee oversaw a mud-wrestling match that troops joined.
explanation.walkthrough: MUD jumbled to UMD takes in PI and RE: UM-PIRE-D.
explanation.definitionFit: To umpire a match is to referee or adjudicate it.

clue.text: Discharge redirected by custom exhausts

parts.note: a use is a custom or habit

indicators.note: redirected means the word for discharge is pointed the other way, read backwards

parts.note: pus is a discharge from a wound

explanation.surface: Something discharged and rerouted by customs officers wears them out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redirected' sends the discharge word backwards; 'by' only places that piece next to the custom word.
explanation.definitionFit: To use up resources is to exhaust or consume them entirely.

clue.text: Smooth jazz singer's embracing power suit

indicators.note: embracing means the singer's name holds the power letter inside

parts.note: Sade is a singer known for smooth jazz-soul, plus the possessive S
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A smooth jazz singer wears a power suit.
explanation.walkthrough: SADES with P embraced after the S gives S-P-ADES.
explanation.definitionFit: Spades is one of the four suits in a pack of cards.

clue.text: Posh golfer held up device looking for clues

indicators.note: held up in a down clue means the pieces are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: U means upper-class, posh
Ernie Els is a South African golfer
a thing is a gadget or device

explanation.surface: An upper-class golfer is delayed by a gadget hunting for leads.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'held up' reads the posh letter and the South African golfer upwards together, before the device follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleuthing means detective work, investigating evidence.

clue.text: Tax system collecting Penny's tips from snack counter

indicators.note: collecting means the tax abbreviation picks up the penny letter inside it

parts.note: PAYE is the UK pay-as-you-earn income tax system
D is the abbreviation for a penny in old British money

indicators.note: tips from means the first and last letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A tax scheme scoops up Penny's tips at the snack bar.
explanation.walkthrough: PAYE takes in D to give PAYDE; S and K are the first and last letters of 'snack'. PAYE is how UK employers deduct income tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A pay desk is a cash counter where customers pay.

clue.text: New dad tricks lady driver

indicators.note: new means the letters are made afresh in another order

explanation.surface: A fresh dad plays tricks on a woman behind the wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: Dick Dastardly is the villainous racer in the cartoon Wacky Races, so 'driver' is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dick Dastardly competes as a cheating motorist in the Wacky Races cartoon.

clue.text: Solver used pencil?

definitions.meaning: Nancy ... is the teenage detective of fiction, a solver of mysteries
to draw is to sketch, as with a pencil, and its past tense fits

explanation.definitionFit: Nancy Drew is a fictional sleuth who solves cases; drawing is sketching, so someone who used a pencil may have sketched.

clue.text: Australian supporter blocking toilet with English magazine

indicators.note: blocking means these letters sit inside the toilet word, stopping it up

parts.note: a privy is an outdoor toilet
a tee supports a golf ball

explanation.surface: An Aussie fan clogs a loo, accompanied by an English periodical.
explanation.walkthrough: PRIVY is opened up by A TEE to give PRIVATEEY, then E finishes it. Private Eye is a British satirical magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Private Eye is a long-running British satirical and current-affairs fortnightly publication.

clue.text: Essentially foulmouthed terms for Mrs Slocombe and her pussy

annotationWithheld.why: Essentially foulmouthed terms for Mrs Slocombe and her pussy (6) = MOUSER: no reading found that builds MOUSER (middle of 'foulmouthed' gives MOU, but nothing in the rest gives SER) and no blog is available to confirm the parse.
annotationWithheld.clue: Essentially foulmouthed terms for Mrs Slocombe and her pussy

clue.text: Translation of Stoker inspiring the French author

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so these letters are taken inside the rearranged name
a translation renders a text in new form, so the letters of the name are rearranged

parts.note: le is the masculine French word for the

explanation.surface: A translation of Bram Stoker's work inspires a French writer.
explanation.walkthrough: STOKER rearranged to KOESTR with LE breathed in gives KOESTLER.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Koestler was a Hungarian-British writer, known for the novel Darkness at Noon.

clue.text: Team part way through busy stage becomes ambitious

indicators.note: part way through means the team word is placed partway into the jumbled letters
busy suggests bustling activity, so the letters of stage are jumbled

parts.note: a side is a team

explanation.surface: A team on a busy stage gains confidence halfway through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'busy' jumbles the letters of 'stage', and 'part way through' sets the team word partway into them rather than at an end.
explanation.definitionFit: To get ideas is an idiom for growing aspirations above one's station.

clue.text: Former club director accepting price paid to overindulge

indicators.note: accepting means the first pieces take the price inside them

parts.note: a spoon was an old wooden golf club
a fee is a price paid

explanation.surface: An ex-club director takes a payment to spoil someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' is an old golf club, not a society; 'accepting' puts the fee inside, just before the director letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To spoon-feed is to pamper or cosset excessively.

clue.text: Deliver twists with the ultimate in cloak and dagger

indicators.note: twists means the word for deliver is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: to rid is to deliver or free from something

indicators.note: the ultimate in points to the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Cloak-and-dagger intrigue delivers twists.
explanation.walkthrough: RID backwards is DIR; K is the last letter of 'cloak'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirk is a short Scottish stabbing knife.

clue.text: Haggard woman engaging old trainer?

indicators.note: engaging means holding within, so the heroine's name takes this letter inside

parts.note: She is the title character of H. Rider Haggard's novel

explanation.surface: A worn-out woman hires a veteran coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haggard' is not 'gaunt' but the novelist H. Rider Haggard, whose She gives SHE around O.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainer is a kind of sports footwear, so it is one example of the wider class.

clue.text: Queen supporting most of Suede and one of The Pretenders?

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue means the next piece sits beneath
most of means the last letter of the leather word is cut away

parts.note: shammy is chamois leather, a soft suede-like leather
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A queen backs most of the band Suede and a member of The Pretenders.
explanation.walkthrough: Suede and The Pretenders look like bands; here suede is chamois leather and a pretender is anyone faking. In a down clue 'supporting' puts the Queen below.
explanation.definitionFit: A shammer is one who fakes, so a pretender in the literal sense.

clue.text: County's opener dropped with series getting tight

parts.note: a string is a series of things in a row

indicators.note: opener dropped means the first letter is removed, as a batsman might be

parts.note: Kent is an English county in the south-east

explanation.surface: A county cricket team's opening batsman is dropped as a series becomes tense.
explanation.walkthrough: KENT, the English county, loses K to give ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Stringent means strict or severe, as tight rules are.

clue.text: Endless dithering unlikely to succeed

indicators.note: unlikely means improbable, so the remaining letters are put in an unexpected order
endless means the word loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Constant indecision is not going to bring success.
explanation.walkthrough: DITHERING loses its first and last letters to ITHERIN, which 'unlikely' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed to a title or estate is to receive it as heir.

clue.text: Wild reindeer striking Rudolph's nose and wanting more

indicators.note: wild means the letters of reindeer run free in a new order
nose means the front letter of the reindeer's name

explanation.surface: A wild reindeer strikes Rudolph on the nose and is hungrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striking' takes away R (Rudolph's first letter) from the letters of REINDEER, and the rest is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Needier is the comparative of needy, lacking more or in greater want.

clue.text: Bloke left before the end of Softly, Softly

parts.note: a gent is a bloke, a man

indicators.note: the end of points to the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A man leaves before the TV series Softly, Softly finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: Softly, Softly was a British TV police drama; Y is the last letter of the first 'Softly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gently is an adverb meaning quietly or with a light touch.

clue.text: War in shot put with equipment scratching the face of Geoff Capes?

indicators.note: shot means broken or ruined, so the letters are scrambled
scratching means crossing out the letter that follows from the word for equipment

parts.note: gear is equipment

indicators.note: the face of means the front letter of the following name

explanation.surface: Shot-putter Geoff Capes injures his face with kit at a wartime shot-put event.
explanation.walkthrough: WAR IN scrambles to RAINW; GEAR loses G (from Geoff) to give EAR. Geoff Capes was a British shot-putter, so 'Capes' looks like his name, not cloaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Capes are cloaks worn in wet weather, examples of waterproof clothing.

clue.text: Mark getting into difficulties producing Genius

indicators.note: getting into means the letter goes inside the word for difficulties

parts.note: holes are tight spots or difficulties
M is short for the old German currency, the mark

explanation.surface: A man named Mark gets into trouble and produces brilliance.
explanation.walkthrough: Sherlock Holmes is the archetypal detective genius, so his name has become a byword for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherlock's name is used generically for a brilliant investigator or clever person.

clue.text: Reveal upset Christmas stocking time

indicators.note: stocking means filling, so the reversed word holds the time letter
upset in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: Noel is Christmas

explanation.surface: A Christmas stocking upset reveals its contents early.
explanation.walkthrough: NOEL upturned is LEON, filled with T: LE-T-ON.
explanation.definitionFit: To let on is an idiom for disclosing a secret.

clue.text: Villa manager not unknown to eat crackers and cheese

indicators.note: to eat means the shortened name takes the word for crackers into it
not means the unknown letter is left out of the manager's name

parts.note: Unai Emery manages Aston Villa football club
Y is an unknown in algebra
crackers means mad, mental

explanation.surface: A football manager snacks on crackers and cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not unknown' drops the algebraic unknown from the Villa manager's name, and 'to eat' has what is left swallow the word for crackers.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmentaler is a Swiss cheese with holes.

clue.text: Follow story on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means we hear the word spoken, not written

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: Listen along to a broadcast tale.
explanation.definitionFit: To tail someone is to shadow them closely.

clue.text: Flight fault caused by flash

definitions.meaning: an overnight flight that leaves passengers bleary
the photographic effect where a camera flash makes pupils glow scarlet

explanation.definitionFit: A red-eye is a late-night airline service; red-eye is also the photo defect from flash reflecting off the retina.

clue.text: We're not sure about concealing drug user

indicators.note: about means the run of letters is read backwards
concealing says the letters lie tucked within these clue words

explanation.surface: Uncertain whether someone is hiding a drug habit.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside 'We're not sure' sits RENOTS, which read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoner is slang for someone who habitually smokes cannabis.
